topic.title: Earth structure, rocks, resources and carbon dioxide
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2026-27 detailed outline only; not explicit in the 2025-26 Year 8 map
topic.overview: Earth materials are continually changed by the rock cycle, but many useful resources are finite on human timescales. Chemistry helps compare extraction, recycling and climate impacts.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Earth has a thin solid crust, a thick mantle and a core rich in iron and nickel.
Igneous rock forms when molten rock cools and solidifies; slower cooling generally gives larger crystals.
Sedimentary rock forms when sediments are deposited, compacted and cemented.
Metamorphic rock forms when existing rock changes under heat and pressure without melting.
Rock-cycle processes include weathering, erosion, deposition, burial, heating, melting, cooling and uplift.
Burning fossil fuels and some land-use changes raise atmospheric carbon dioxide, strengthening the greenhouse effect; recycling can reduce extraction and energy use but also has costs.

workedExamples.prompt: Magma cools slowly underground. Predict crystal size.
workedExamples.answer: Relatively large crystals because particles have more time to form an ordered crystal structure.

workedExamples.prompt: Give two benefits of recycling aluminium.
workedExamples.answer: Less ore extraction and usually less energy use than extracting new aluminium; it can also reduce waste.

practicals.title: Cooling rate and crystal-size model
practicals.aim: Model how cooling rate affects crystal size using a safe crystallising substance.
practicals.variables: IV: cooling condition; DV: mean crystal size; controls: solution concentration/volume/container and starting temperature.
practicals.method: Prepare equal saturated samples, cool one slowly and one rapidly, allow crystals to form, measure several crystals and calculate means.
practicals.expectedResult: Slower cooling usually produces larger crystals in the model.
practicals.safety: Wear eye protection and use teacher-approved substance; take care with hot solutions and glassware.
practicals.evaluation: Use multiple crystals and repeats, define a consistent size measure and note limitations of a model for magma.

commonMistakes: Saying the mantle is liquid magma everywhere.
Saying metamorphic rock melts before forming.
Claiming recycling has no energy or transport cost.
examTips: For a rock, name starting material, process and product.
For environmental evaluation, give both benefit and limitation.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.title: Cooling rate and crystal-size model
practicals.aim: Model how cooling rate affects crystal size using a safe crystallising substance.
practicals.variables: IV: cooling condition; DV: mean crystal size; controls: solution concentration/volume/container and starting temperature.
practicals.method: Prepare equal saturated samples, cool one slowly and one rapidly, allow crystals to form, measure several crystals and calculate means.
practicals.expectedResult: Slower cooling usually produces larger crystals in the model.
practicals.safety: Wear eye protection and use teacher-approved substance; take care with hot solutions and glassware.
practicals.evaluation: Use multiple crystals and repeats, define a consistent size measure and note limitations of a model for magma.
